name: pdk-linref-dataframe
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our road inventory now includes point survey observations as well as road ranges. Calling `linref.integrate` in `/app` on their LRS configured pandas frames with `split_at_locs=True` should return the least common road intervals, with an inverse column for each input. A sample is in `/data/survey/road-ranges.csv` and `/data/survey/observations.csv`. Right now the observations disappear from the inverse columns even when the intervals split.

The first input is a linear road frame. A point at an interval's beginning belongs to that interval, not the one before it. Points beyond road coverage do not extend the output; with `fill_gaps=False`, intervals with no road range are omitted. With `expand=False`, choose the first matching row in source order from each input; with `expand=True`, retain every combination of overlapping ranges and observations, including separate observations at the same site. An unmatched input gets a missing inverse value. Keep original index labels without converting numeric or text labels, and retain the caller's inverse column names. An empty observation frame should behave like one with no matches. Repeated calls on unchanged frames should return the same rows. Please fix this without breaking the existing range only integration behavior. The environment is offline with pandas, geopandas and the package installed.

name: pdk-libresvip-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our contributors send vocal parts as UST files, and we import them with LibreSVIP's UST plugin, `get_svs_plugin_by_suffix("ust").load(path, options)` from `libresvip.extension.manager`. Since most of them moved to newer editors, the imports go wrong: garbled lyrics, files that won't load, and a tempo entry for nearly every note. Last week's files are in /data/ust/.

Every one of them should import with the lyrics and timing the singer meant. A file that declares its charset with a Charset= line, or starts with a UTF-8 byte order mark, must be decoded that way whatever the `encoding` option says. The option is only for files that declare nothing. Bytes that aren't valid in the charset that applies should make `load` raise UnicodeDecodeError, not return replacement characters.

`song_tempo_list` should have one entry per real tempo change, the first at tick 0. A Tempo= on a note or rest takes effect where it starts, and 120 BPM is only for files with no tempo at all. Each note's lyric should be just the syllable that's sung. Rests, however they're written, must not become notes, and no other note moves or changes length. A sung note with no NoteNum is still a ValueError.

A UST exported by this plugin, with any `encoding` option, has to load back to the same project. The existing tests and the checks in /app/AGENTS.md must keep passing. There's no network, and everything is installed in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-dedupe-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our CRM merge now sends alternate spellings of a field as a list of strings, and dedupe breaks on it. A sample batch is in `/data/profiles/merge.json`. We match name as String, nick as ShortString and tags as Set.

`dedupe.canonicalize(cluster)` should return one string for every field in any record, in first seen order: the spelling with the lowest average normalized affine gap distance to the spellings the records give, the first one on a tie, or "" when there is none. Empty strings and empty lists give nothing, and a record repeating a spelling shouldn't change the result. Clusters of plain strings must keep their current results. An empty cluster raises `ValueError`; a value that isn't a string or a list of strings raises `TypeError`.

When scoring pairs, a String or ShortString field should count as its closest pair of spellings, one from each record, and a field with no spelling as missing, like None. The fingerprinter should give a record every block key one of its spellings would get on its own, index predicates included, also after `reset_indices` and indexing another batch, and raise `TypeError` for a list member that isn't a string. A list in a Set field is one set of tokens and must score and block exactly like the same tuple. Then `prepare_training`, `train` and `partition` should work on the merge.

Calls must not share state. Could you find and fix this? The package and pytest are installed in `/app`, and there's no network.

name: pdk-parsimonious-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our validation jobs load their grammars with parsimonious (the checkout in /app). The language team now writes every grammar in the PEG notation of Bryan Ford's 2004 paper, since the same files feed their C tools, and Grammar() rejects them. Some of them are in /data/peg, each with a folder of the same name holding texts it must accept. peg.peg is the notation's own grammar, and every .peg file there has to parse with it.

Please make Grammar() take that notation as it is: rules defined with `<-`, `'...'` and `"..."` literals and `[...]` classes with the paper's escapes, and `.`. A grammar written that way must load and parse exactly as the same grammar written in parsimonious's notation would, with the same rules matching the same spans of every text and the same errors. Classes and `.` should also work, the same way, in parsimonious's own notation. A grammar that uses both `=` and `<-`, or a class with a reversed range such as `[z-a]`, should raise BadGrammar.

We send merged grammars back to the team, so str() of a grammar loaded from that notation (also after .default()) has to print it in the paper's notation, in a form that loads back into the same grammar.

Grammars in parsimonious's notation have to load, parse and print exactly as they do now, and the existing tests in /app/parsimonious/tests have to keep passing. There's no network here, and the package is installed in editable mode in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-clevercsv-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our supplier now starts some CSV exports with a line like sep=; that names the delimiter, sometimes after a UTF-8 BOM. That line isn't a data row, and only the first line of a file has this meaning. Real exports are in /data/exports, and clevercsv should read each as exactly the cells of the sheet. Please fix this.

It should work in read_table, stream_table, read_dicts, stream_dicts, read_dataframe, detect_dialect, Sniffer().sniff and has_header on an export's text, and the detect, standardize and code commands of python -m clevercsv. The declared delimiter always wins, even in a file with only that line or over a caller's dialect (whose other settings still apply). Quote and escape characters are detected from the rest, and has_header judges the rows after the line. standardize (stdout, -o, -i with its usual exit codes, -t) and the code that code prints (also with -p) give the rows without that line. An export with a sep line and a BOM reads the same with or without encoding="utf-8".

If the first line starts with sep= but names no delimiter, a double quote, or two different characters (one repeated character still names it), the functions raise ValueError and the commands exit non-zero, leaving the file unchanged. Invalid UTF-8 still raises UnicodeDecodeError with encoding="utf-8". Files without a sep line behave as today. Reading a file again, also after rows were appended, gives each row once, in file order.

Use /opt/venv/bin/python in /app. There's no network. The exis

name: pdk-dbt-stripe-dbt
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Stripe's export now sends a record again whenever it changes, and the dbt project in /app shows stale billing totals and extra rows. A sample of the new export is in /data/stripe_export, in the columns of the seeds in /app/integration_tests/seeds.

Every report should look as if only the last synced version of each invoice and of each invoice line had ever been sent, also when a correction lowers an amount. The same line id on two invoices is two lines. That covers stripe__invoice_line_item_details, stripe__invoice_details, stripe__subscription_details and stripe__line_item_enhanced, its line rows and its header rows' total_amount, which is the invoice total minus its line amounts. Temporary lines still stay out. Lines with an empty unique_id are normal lines, so number_of_line_items and avg_num_line_items count each current line of an invoice once.

We're also adding a second Stripe connection through the package's stripe_sources variable. Records from different connections never replace each other, and every report keeps them apart by source_relation.

A rebuild after more versions arrive must match a clean build on the whole export. Keep every model's columns, and the integration project must still build on its own seeds with its data tests passing. The project stays SQL: only SQL models, macros and YAML, with no Python models.

I run dbt seed --full-refresh and then dbt build in /app/integration_tests, with a DuckDB profile whose schema is stripe_integrations_tests. dbt,

name: pdk-dbt-openai-dbt
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Since we moved nightly jobs to the Batch API and put a few projects on flex and priority processing, `openai__cost_usage_report` from the dbt package in /app no longer adds up per project. A project that only runs batch jobs is charged a blended rate. A sample of November's `completion` and `cost` tables is in /data/openai.

The report needs a `service_tier` column (`default`, `flex`, `priority` or `batch`; Batch API usage is `batch`) and one row per day, project, model, tier and token unit type. Every usage row and token cost line item belongs to one of those tiers; `other` rows keep a null tier. Cost the export ties to a project stays `direct`. Cost without a project is spread only over usage of the same day, model, unit and tier, from projects with no direct cost there. Usage or cost with no counterpart in its own tier is its own `unmatched` row, never priced at another tier's rate, and the report must still tie out to the cost table. The same column and grain apply when only the cost or only the completion table is enabled.

The project in /app/integration_tests (profile `integration_tests` is set up for a local DuckDB file; run `dbt seed` before `dbt build`) must keep building on its own seeds, which have no tier columns, with every data test passing. The project stays SQL: the change goes in SQL models, macros and YAML, with no Python models. There's no network; dbt-core and dbt-duckdb are installed.

name: pdk-yato-pipeline
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We run yato every night against the DuckDB file dlt loads into. dlt writes the raw schema, then `yato run` builds our models into the transform schema. The morning tables are often wrong. Some models get built before the models they read, so they fail on a missing table or quietly use the previous night's data. And when a model breaks (last night, a bad amount in the payments load), the run finishes as if everything worked and the models reading it are rebuilt from old data.

A copy of the warehouse right after tonight's dlt load is at /data/warehouse.duckdb, and our models are in /data/models.

Every model has to be built after every model its query reads, the way DuckDB resolves the names when yato runs it, whatever `--schema` is. That goes for SQL models and for what a Python model's source_sql reads.

If a model fails, it and every model reading it, directly or through other models, should keep what they held before the run (or stay missing if they never existed), and every other model should still be built. Then the run should fail: `Yato.run()` raises an exception naming every model that failed, and `yato run` prints those names and exits non-zero. A Python model that raises counts as failed, like a SQL model.

Could you find what's wrong in /app and fix it? The existing tests in /app/tests have to keep passing. There's no network here, and yato's dependencies are installed.

name: pdk-parsedatetime-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our webhook ingest runs each delivery's `sent_at` through `Calendar().parseDT(value, sourceTime=..., tzinfo=...)` and its free text `note` through `Calendar().nlp(note, sourceTime=...)`, using parsedatetime in /app. Since our partners changed formats the results are wrong. ISO timestamps like `2026-10-05T14:30:00+02:00` come back with the year read as a time of day, offsets get dropped or read as an hour, and email dates like `Sun, 04 Oct 2026 23:59:59 GMT` land on the wrong day. Monday's deliveries are in /data/webhooks/deliveries-2026-10-05.jsonl.

Every `sent_at` there is valid, and parseDT should return the exact instant it names, converted to the tzinfo we pass, or without one as an aware datetime with the timestamp's own offset. Fractions of a second may be kept or dropped, and the context should report a date and a time. A timestamp without an offset gives its wall clock with the tzinfo attached, as today. One that can't exist (Feb 30, 25:10, offset +25:00) should come back like unreadable text, as the sourceTime with a context holding no date or time.

nlp() should report each such timestamp in a note as one match covering exactly its text, with the datetime parseDT gives for it, and leave the note's other matches as they are. We reuse one Calendar for the whole feed, so no result may depend on earlier ones. The existing tests in /app/tests must keep passing. There's no network here.

name: pdk-gtfparse-dataframe
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our annotation is the Ensembl GTF plus two exon-only GTFs from the lab: a long-read transcript catalog and the ERCC spike-ins. We cat the three files together and run

```python
df = read_gtf("/data/annotation/combined.gtf")
df = create_missing_features(
    df,
    unique_keys={"gene": "gene_id", "transcript": "transcript_id"},
    extra_columns={
        "gene": {"gene_name", "gene_biotype", "gene_version"},
        "transcript": {"gene_id", "gene_name", "transcript_name", "transcript_biotype",
                       "transcript_version", "protein_id"},
    },
)
```

so pyensembl gets gene and transcript rows. Samples of all four files are in /data/annotation. read_gtf fails on the combined file, and when we read the files one by one and pd.concat them instead, the lab's genes still get no gene or transcript rows.

read_gtf on the combined file should give the same rows as reading each file alone. After create_missing_features, every row with a gene_id should sit inside exactly one gene row with that gene_id, chromosome and strand, and the same goes for transcript_id and transcript rows. Rows already in the input stay as they are. Each added row spans exactly the rows it covers, has source gtfparse and no score, and its extra columns hold the value those rows agree on, ignoring rows without that attribute, or stay empty when they disagree. The result keeps the input's columns and their types (categoricals stay categoricals, integers stay integers) for any index, including a

name: pdk-parquetdb-schema
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our results store is a ParquetDB dataset (the library is checked out in /app) filled from our v1 exports. The v2 exports renamed some fields: `e_form` is now `formation_energy`, `magmom` is now `total_magnetization`, and the nested `sample` record is now `specimen`. On a copy, `rename_fields` leaves the new fields empty and keeps the old ones. The store is in /data/store/results and the exports still to load are in /data/exports.

After `db.rename_fields(name_map)`, every record should have its value under the new name, keeping its type and field metadata, and the old name should be gone. Dataset metadata and other fields stay as they were. A key is a field name as `read()` shows it (dotted for sub-fields) or a nested record's name, which moves all of its sub-fields. Some v2 exports were already loaded, so a new name can already exist. Then the result is one field holding every record's value, typed as `create` would type both (whole numbers and floats give floats). If a record has values under both names, or a name was never in the store, raise ValueError and leave the store as it was.

Old names must keep working, also from a new `ParquetDB` on the same path and after a field is renamed again. Every export in /data/exports should load through `create` with all values under the new names, and `update` should accept old names too. Running the same rename again changes nothing.

There's no network, and the dependencies are installed in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-bitstring-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our controller team now generates telemetry record layouts from their C headers as struct format strings. Our decoder hands each layout to bitstring, since the records also carry bit fields between the structs, like `<IHH?x, u3, bool, u4, <8s?`. bitstring only knows the numeric struct codes, so most layouts fail. Monday's captures, the layouts and our scripts are in /data/telemetry.

A struct group is `<`, `>` or `!` followed by any codes struct accepts after them, with counts as struct uses them. Wherever a group sits in a format (a string or a list, with repeats, brackets and keyword lengths) and at whatever bit position, `Bits.unpack`, `Reader.read_list` and `pack` should give exactly what `struct.unpack` and `struct.pack` give for it. A single code holding one value, such as `<?` or `!12p`, should read and write the same way anywhere a dtype is accepted, `Array` included, as `>h` already does.

Out of range integers, a str or int for `s` or `p`, and `c` bytes that aren't one byte long should raise `ValueError`. A record that runs past the end of the data raises `ReadError` and leaves the Reader where it was. `@`, `=` and codes with only a native size still raise `ValueError`.

/data/telemetry/replay_setpoints.py packs Monday's setpoints, and every record it packs should match the controllers' echo and trend files byte for byte.

Keep the existing tests in /app/tests passing and follow /app/AGENTS.md for docs and release notes. There's no network; everything is installed i

name: pdk-target-csv-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Since our shop tap moved to the vendor's new API, the CSVs target-csv in /app writes are a mess. The tap now sends a new SCHEMA mid-run whenever the API adds or drops a field, and we run it hourly into the same folder with `overwrite_behavior: append_records`, `load_method: upsert` and `batch_size_rows` set. Values land under the wrong column, earlier hours vanish, orders repeat, and one run crashed. Three hourly tap outputs are in /data/tap-output/.

Each file should have one header with every column it has had. Columns already there keep their place, and new ones go after them in the order they first show up. Every value sits under its own column (empty where a record lacks it), and fields missing from the stream's current schema are left out. A run writes one file per stream, also when `file_naming_scheme` uses `{timestamp}`.

With upsert, each order should be in orders.csv once, as the tap last sent it, and the same goes for any stream with key properties. Streams without key properties, and the default `load_method`, keep every record. With `append_records`, running the hourly outputs one after another must leave the same files as one run over all of them, and `replace_file`, the default, still starts each run over. Rows from earlier runs keep their exact values under any `encoding` and `escape_character`. If an existing file can't be read, the run should fail and leave it untouched.

Please fix it. The existing tests in /app/tests must keep passing. There's no network h

name: pdk-puremagic-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We're running a legacy document archive through an ingest job that routes every file on `puremagic.from_file()`, and a lot of it comes back as the wrong type. It's old Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Outlook files of every size. A sample of the export is in `/data/dms-export/`.

Each of these files should come back as what it is: `.doc`, `.xls`, `.ppt` or `.msg`, with the same MIME types puremagic reports today for the files in `/app/test/resources/office`, and Word templates as `.dot` with `application/msword`. The answer has to come from the content, since many files reach the job under names that say nothing about their type.

Our queue worker only has the bytes. For these files, `from_string(data)`, `from_stream(fh)`, `magic_string(data)` and `magic_stream(fh)` called without a filename should give the same answers as `from_file` and `magic_file` give for the same bytes on disk, also when the same stream is checked more than once.

Some files in the archive are cut short or corrupt. When a file is cut short, or its internal sector references loop or point past the end of the file, `from_file`, `from_string` and `from_stream` should raise `puremagic.PureError` instead of guessing, and they must never hang.

Other files must identify through `from_file` exactly as they do today. The tests in `/app/test`, `ruff check` and `ty check` have to stay clean, and a changelog entry, if you add one, should follow the repo's changelog rules. There's no network; the project's dev tools are

name: pdk-graflo-pipeline
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We run graflo's ingest every night over HR's exports into a file backend directory, and the analytics team reads that directory as our org graph. The setup is in /data/hr: manifest.yaml, snapshot.yaml and the last three nights under /data/hr/exports. The first night ran with `--fresh-start true`, and each later night runs from its own export folder:

```
cd /data/hr/exports/2026-10-06
python -m graflo.cli.ingest --db-config-path /data/hr/snapshot.yaml --schema-path /data/hr/manifest.yaml
```

The directory has turned into a pile of copies. People show up once per night and per file that mentions them, old versions sit next to new ones, and edges repeat the same way.

After each night the directory should hold the graph as HR has it that night, stored the way a database would: every vertex once per identity, each person with the name, email, title and department HR has for them, and every edge once per pair of endpoints with its latest properties. That shouldn't depend on `--batch-size`, and running the same night twice in a row should leave the same graph. INDEX.json must list exactly the chunk files in the directory with their real record counts, no chunk may hold more than `chunk_size` records, and `--fresh-start true` should still start from an empty graph.

Could you find what's wrong in graflo and fix it? The tests in /app/test and the project's ruff and ty checks should keep passing. There's no network here; everything is installed in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-diffly-dataframe
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our nightly check compares the previous and the current export of hourly meter readings with `diffly <previous>.parquet <current>.parquet --primary-key meter_id --primary-key reading_start --json`. This week the export job moved to a new Parquet writer. It stores the readings with different column types, and since then the check fails with a PrimaryKeyError or a polars error before it reports anything. Two exports a day apart, one from each writer, are in /data/exports.

The comparison should come out exactly as it would if the new file's values had first been converted to the old file's column types: the same rows matched by key, the same rows only on one side, and the same match rates and changed values in every column, with abs_tol, rel_tol and abs_tol_temporal working as before. The one difference is that diffly should still report the changed column types. This has to hold whichever export is passed as left, through compare_frames, the CLI and diffly.testing.assert_frame_equal with check_dtypes=False. Key columns of different kinds, like text against numbers, should still raise PrimaryKeyError.

Please keep to /app/AGENTS.md, so the existing tests and the pre-commit checks (ruff, ruff format, mypy, docformatter, typos, license headers, whitespace) must still pass. There's no network; everything diffly needs is installed in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-tap-weatherapi-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We run tap-weatherapi from /app with use_bulk_requests and a locations_file of a few hundred sites, and the historical stream doesn't keep track of the sites separately. A site we add to the file is never backfilled, and when a site comes back with an error or with fewer days than the rest, the days it missed are never asked for again. Turning bulk requests off doesn't help either, since then every run asks for everything from start_date again. Our locations file, the state our last run saved and that run's bulk response are in /data/weatherapi/.

In both modes, each location should only be asked for the days after its own bookmark (the last day it actually got, or start_date if it has none) up to the end date, and not at all once it's up to date. No location's day should be asked for or emitted twice in one run. A state saved in either mode has to work in the other. The state our bulk runs have saved so far has to carry over too, so every location continues after that bookmark, and a site added to the file later is backfilled from start_date.

In bulk mode every history request must still be a POST with at most bulk_request_chunk_size locations and at most 30 days, and locations that need the same days should go out together.

Could you fix this? The existing tests, ruff, mypy and ty must keep passing. There's no network here.

name: pdk-gspread-pandas-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our Berlin, Paris and Zurich offices now paste their exports into their own intake spreadsheets, each set to the office's locale, and we read them with `sheet_to_df(convert_types=True)`. The types come out wrong: 1.234,56 turns into 1.23456, 2,5 into 25, the Paris amounts and WAHR/FALSCH stay text, and a French 03/04/2026 becomes the 4th of March. What the Sheets API returns for each office's tab is in /data/intake.

Every converted value should be what the person who typed it meant, with the types an English (US) sheet gets today: columns of whole numbers as integers, columns with decimals as floats, dates as datetimes, and WAHR/FALSCH and VRAI/FAUX as booleans like TRUE/FALSE. Dates written like 31.12.2026 are day first, with or without a time. When every value in a column could be read either way (decimal point or decimal comma, day or month first), it should follow the spreadsheet's locale. `gspread_pandas.clean.convert_types` on a plain DataFrame has no locale and keeps today's reading for those (decimal point, month first). A column that mixes the two ways stays text, like any column with a value that won't convert, and neither `apply_types` nor the model's type suggestions (when GSPREAD_PANDAS_AI_API_KEY is set) may convert a column more loosely than that.

English sheets have to come out exactly as they do today, the existing tests in /app/tests have to keep passing, and changes should pass black, isort and flake8 as /app/CONTRIBUTING.rst asks. There's no network here

name: pdk-iceberg-loader-schema
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our daily order exports are Arrow IPC streams that we load into Iceberg with `load_ipc_stream_to_iceberg(path, ('shop', 'orders'), catalog, LoaderConfig(write_mode='append', schema_evolution=True))`. The shop backend moved to a new exporter on 5 October, and since then some loads fail and others store numbers that aren't what was exported. Exports from before and after the switch are in /data/exports/.

With schema_evolution on, every value of every export, old or new, should read back from the table exactly as exported, and a value an export doesn't have should read back as NULL. A column whose type arrives wider in a way Iceberg allows (int to long, float to double, more decimal digits at the same scale) should be widened in place, keeping the rows already there, and loading an older export afterwards must not narrow it again. Loading the exports file by file, or all their batches in one `load_batches_to_iceberg` call with any `commit_interval`, should give the same table.

When a column keeps its type (schema_evolution off, or a change Iceberg can't make), a value the column can't hold exactly, such as a whole number out of range, a fraction for a whole number column, a decimal with too many digits or text that isn't a number, should be stored as NULL while the other values still load. Floats are still rounded to the column's precision.

The existing tests in /app/tests, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `ty check` should keep passing. There's no network, and the dep

name: pdk-dbt-hubspot-dbt
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our HubSpot connector changed how it delivers email events. The email event export now sends some rows more than once, and corrects events later under the same id: a later row can change an event's type, send, created time or recipient, mark it filtered, or set obsoleted_by_id. The row with the latest `_fivetran_synced` is the event's current state. A sample of the new exports is in `/data/hubspot_export/`. The email reports of the package in `/app` now count rows instead of events.

Please fix the package so every report reflects current events. In `hubspot__email_sends`, `opens`, `clicks`, `bounces` and `deliveries` should count each current event of that type once, under its current send, and `was_opened` and `was_clicked` should follow them. Filtered and obsolete events count nowhere, in any report. Each send should appear once, with its newest details.

The models `hubspot__email_event_sent`, `hubspot__email_event_delivered`, `hubspot__email_event_opens`, `hubspot__email_event_clicks` and `hubspot__email_event_bounce` should list each event once, only under its current type, with its current `email_send_id` and `created_timestamp` and its newest details from that type's export. They still list filtered and obsolete events, as the README says. A row whose id isn't in the email event export stays listed as it is today.

The `total_` and `total_unique_` columns for those four counts in `hubspot__email_campaigns` and `hubspot__contacts` should agree with the fixed sends. In

name: pdk-sqlite-history-json-schema
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We track SQLite tables with sqlite-history-json (/app) and have since changed some: columns added with ALTER TABLE ADD COLUMN, columns and tables renamed with ALTER TABLE RENAME while tracking was on, and columns dropped by disabling tracking, dropping and enabling again. Now restore returns NULLs or fails with "no such column" and history on a renamed table fails, but `python -m sqlite_history_json.upgrade` says there's nothing to upgrade. A copy of the database is at /data/shop.db.

After the upgrade, restoring a table that has tracking on to its latest entry should give exactly its current rows, and later changes should be recorded as on a table tracked from scratch. Existing entries keep their id, timestamp, operation, primary key and group, with each value under the current name of the column it was recorded from, in history, row-history, restore and row-state-sql. Values for dropped columns stay in the history and restore ignores them. A renamed table's history follows it, so everything works under the new name, enable and disable included.

Tables with tracking off and history of dropped tables stay as they are. A second run changes nothing. With --dry-run it lists only the tables it would change and changes nothing. If a renamed table's new name already has its own history, the upgrade exits with an error naming the table and changes nothing. Databases from 0.3 and earlier must still upgrade, and the tests in /app/tests must keep passing.

name: pdk-osm2geojson-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
We used to pull a fresh Overpass extract (`out meta`) every hour and convert it with osm2geojson. Now we pull the extract once a day and, during the day, download every changeset closed since then from the OSM API as an osmChange file, one file per changeset. A sample is in /data/overpass: that morning's extract and the day's changeset files.

osm2geojson can't use those files yet. `xml2geojson` and `json2geojson` should take a `changes` keyword, a list of osmChange documents as strings, and return the same GeoJSON you'd get by converting, with the same options, a fresh extract taken after all of those changesets. The command line should do the same with `python -m osm2geojson EXTRACT OUTFILE --changes FILE [FILE ...]`, for OSM XML and Overpass JSON extracts. Without changes everything should work as it does now, and `json2geojson` still mustn't modify the dict it's given.

If a change isn't a well formed osmChange document, both functions should raise `ValueError`, and the command line should print an error naming that file to stderr, exit with status 1 and not write the output file.

`ruff check .`, `ruff format --check .`, `mypy osm2geojson` and the tests in /app/tests have to keep passing. There's no network here; the dev tools are installed.

name: pdk-glom-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our vendor's order export is now JSON Lines, and we reshape it with `python -m glom` and our existing specs. A few days of the vendor's files are in /data/exports/, and they have to go through as they come.

Please add `jsonl` as a target format. Each nonblank line is its own JSON document, and the spec runs on each one with the usual glom behavior. Print one result per line, in input order, with no surrounding array. Blank and whitespace-only lines print nothing. The other targets keep their whole-document behavior, and the `json` target has to read the vendor's daily summary files. Files and standard input both have to work.

We also pipe the live export in (`tail -f orders.jsonl | python -m glom --target-format jsonl id | head -3`). Each result has to be printed as soon as its line arrives, and once whatever reads the output stops, the command should end quietly with nothing on stderr. With `--scalar`, each output line should be exactly what the `json` target prints for that document alone, and `--indent` never splits a result over several lines.

If a line is bad (malformed JSON, text that can't be decoded, or the spec fails on it), the earlier lines' results should still be printed. Then the command stops with a nonzero exit status and an error on stderr naming the line, like `line 12`, counted the way `sed -n 12p` counts.

There's no network here, and everything is installed in /app.

name: pdk-open-auto-loader-pipeline
instruction_first_1500_chars:
After every delivery from our POS vendor we load their drop with OpenAutoLoader, using the default CSV settings.

```python
OpenAutoLoader(source="/data/drop", target="/data/warehouse/orders",
               check_point="/data/warehouse/state", schema_path="/data/warehouse/state").run(batch_id=delivery_date)
```

Since the vendor moved to a new export system, the Delta table no longer matches their reports. Some days never show up, and corrected exports keep the old numbers. When they correct an export they upload it again under the same name, and every night they upload the last two days again whether anything changed or not. This week's drop is in /data/drop, and /data/warehouse has the table, checkpoint and schema contract our current version left.

After every run the table should hold the rows of every export in the drop exactly once, as the export reads now. A corrected export replaces the rows it loaded before and no others. An export uploaded again unchanged isn't loaded again, so its rows keep their `_batch_id`. Rows of exports that later leave the drop stay.

If an export can't be read or fails the schema check, `run()` should raise an error naming the export's path, without touching the rows already in the table. A later run picks the export up once it's fixed.

Checkpoints written by the current version, like the one in /data/warehouse, have to keep working. The first run after the upgrade should leave every export's current rows in the table once, and later runs

name: pdk-xlrd-etl
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Since this week a vendor's BIFF8 XLS export breaks `xlrd.open_workbook`. A sample is at `/data/ledger-2026-10-05.xls`. The export divides long text among CONTINUE records: shared strings with their formatting runs and phonetic data, the cached text results of formula cells, and cell comments.

Every piece of text should come back exactly as the vendor wrote it, wherever the records are cut; a formula's text result or a comment should read the same as that text would as a shared string, and no other cell may be lost or changed. With `formatting_info=True`, `Sheet.rich_text_runlist_map` must keep each shared string's `(character offset, font index)` runs, and every comment in `Sheet.cell_note_map` must keep its `text` and `rich_text_runlist`. Phonetic data must never become part of the next string or shift its runs. All of this must also hold with `on_demand=True`, with sheets loaded in any order, unloaded and loaded again, and when the same export is opened again.

Incomplete or invalid text data in any of these places, and a cell that refers to a shared string past the end of the table, must raise `xlrd.biffh.XLRDError`, not a decoding, indexing, unpacking or assertion error. Ordinary XLS files must keep their values and types.

Could you find what's going wrong and fix it? The repository is in `/app`, with Python 3.12 and its dependencies installed. There's no network, and the existing `/app/tests` suite should still pass.

name: pdk-pyfunctional-pipeline
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our nightly job loads the carrier's shipment feed into SQLite with PyFunctional, one call per daily file, like `seq.jsonl(path).to_sqlite3(db_path, "shipments")`. Since the carrier moved to a new export system the job keeps breaking. Three days of the new feed are in /data/shipments/; could you find what's wrong and fix it?

Every daily file has to load, in any order, into the table the earlier days made. With a table name and dict or namedtuple records, `to_sqlite3` should create a missing table and add a column, named exactly like the field, for every field the table lacks. A record without a field reads NULL there. In columns made this way, every str, int, float and None value must come back from `seq.sqlite3` with the same type and value. When the table has a primary key, a record whose key is already there replaces that row.

A call that fails part way (a value SQLite can't store, a line cut short, the sequence raising) must raise and leave the database as it was, even if the caller commits afterwards. Paths, connections and cursors should all work, with table names or INSERT statements, and a successful call is committed. Backfills run several calls at once, in separate processes on one database file; each must succeed and leave the same table as running them one after another.

The existing tests in /app/functional/test must keep passing, and pylint, black and mypy must stay clean on /app/functional. There's no network; dev tools are in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-imessage-conversation-analyzer-dataframe
instruction_first_1500_chars:
The reaction numbers ica gives me are off for my newer conversations. When someone takes back a tapback, the "Removed a heart from …" line counts as a message, and when someone changes a heart to a thumbs up, both count. A friend's phone is set to Spanish, so their tapbacks count as messages, and a reply I typed as Loved “Dune” counts as a reaction.

The messages frame from `ica.get_dataframes()` should match what the conversation shows in Messages today. `is_reaction` should be true for exactly the tapbacks, whatever language their text is in, and also when a row has no text. Only tapbacks that are still showing should be rows: each person has at most one tapback on a message, the one they left last, and a tapback they took back is gone. The removal lines are never rows. This has to hold with a date range too: a tapback that was changed or taken back after the end of the range doesn't count, and the range itself keeps working as it does now. `message_totals` and the other analyzers read that frame.

A copy of my Messages database is at /data/Library/Messages/chat.db, with my Contacts database under /data/Library, laid out as in my home folder. Databases from older macOS versions that don't record tapback details should keep working as they do today, and the checks in /app/AGENTS.md should still pass. There's no network here; the project's dependencies, ruff and ty are installed in /opt/venv.

name: pdk-sdmxthon-dataframe
instruction_first_1500_chars:
Our reporting agents moved to the new collection platform, and sdmxthon mishandles its SDMX-CSV 2.0 uploads. A few of this week's uploads are in /data/uploads/, and the BIS structures they use are in /data/structures/bis_structures.xml.

Some uploads don't read at all with read_sdmx or get_pandas_df. The rest come back changed, with codes and numbers rewritten, and in an upload with several dataflows each dataflow's table picks up the other dataflows' columns. get_datasets(upload, "/data/structures/bis_structures.xml") has the same problems and also treats the platform's attribute rows as observations.

Every upload like these should read, from its path or its text. Each dataflow is its own dataset, keyed by its STRUCTURE_ID, with all of its rows and only the columns that have a value in them. Every value stays exactly as the file has it, as text, and only an empty cell is missing (NaN). A row with more cells than the header should raise a ValueError.

From get_datasets, a dataset holds observations only. A row that leaves some of its dimensions empty isn't an observation. Its attribute values apply to every observation matching the dimensions it fills in, and a row with no dimension filled in holds dataset attributes, which go into attached_attributes instead of the data. Writing such a dataset with to_sdmx_csv(2) and reading that text back with get_datasets should give the same dataset.
